reading.body:
Hillary Scholten's AI record is legislative and financial, not rhetorical: 13 of 20 dated events are bills she sponsored or cosponsored, and 5 are $1,000 PAC contributions.

The bills cluster around two subjects. One is data center siting and resource disclosure, including the Responsible Data Center Siting Act, the Data Center Resource Disclosure Act, and the Defending Our Energy and Water Act, all dated July to September 2026. The other is small business AI adoption and model documentation, including the AI-WISE Act, the SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act, and the READ AI Models Act. The first cluster is the one that touches the site's core claim: siting and resource disclosure bills are about where compute gets built and what it consumes, which is the building-and-power layer rather than the model layer.

The money is small and concentrated. Four of the five contributions are $1,000 from Amazon's separate segregated fund, dated May 2025 through August 2026, and one is $1,000 from Google's NetPAC in November 2025. The data does not show total fundraising, committee balances, or any contribution above $1,000, so it cannot support a claim about the scale of industry money in this record. It also does not show whether any contribution preceded, followed, or related to any bill, and the page states that placement in date order is not a claim of causation.

Three recorded votes appear, and two of them are absences: she voted absent on H.R. 7757 in June 2026 and on H.R. 5764 in January 2026, a bill she herself sponsored. The only recorded yea is on S. 146 in April 2025. The data covers only events this site holds, so it is a partial record, and it says nothing about committee assignments, floor statements, or positions taken outside these filings.
